$schema.purpose: The design taxonomy: what things ARE. Concepts linked by pp:isA, each declaring the parts and the motion that are true at its own level, so anything below inherits them.
$schema.scope: A concept is anything the design graph names. Two branches hang off the root and they are not the same kind of thing: pp:Thing is DEPICTABLE — it can be drawn, it has parts and a rig — while pp:Criterion is EVALUATIVE — it is how work is judged and carries no geometry. Mixing them in one tree was the temptation; a rubric axis has no parts and a pigeon has no verdict. pp:Domain is the third: what KIND of work a piece is, which is what makes gold comparable — a typographic exemplar says nothing about an illustration.

edges.pp:isA: the parent concept. Parts, rig and match terms accumulate up this chain, nearest ancestor winning on a conflict.
edges.pp:hasPart: a part that exists at THIS level. Declared once, on the most general concept it is true of: a beak belongs to pp:Bird, a collar to pp:Pigeon.

fields.id: the concept's `pp:` id, and its identity in the graph
fields.match: phrases in a brief that name this concept; the longest match across the whole taxonomy wins
fields.hasPart: { id, z } — z is paint order within the assembly, back to front
fields.rig: { part, property, amplitude, durationMs, easing } — amplitude is a FRACTION of the part's own span for x/y and DEGREES for rotation, so motion holds at any drawn size. Declared at the level where it is true of every descendant.

concepts.label: Concept
concepts.note: The root of everything the graph names, depictable or not.

concepts.label: Thing
concepts.note: Depictable. Everything under this can be drawn: it has parts, and it may have a rig.

rig.note: The tail flicks about its own root.
A pigeon bobs fore and aft: the head thrusts forward and the body catches up.
The beak sits on the head and carries the head's throw exactly.
The neck follows the head at a fraction of the throw.

channels.name: bob
channels.note: The head thrusts FORWARD and the body catches up — that is the whole of a pigeon's walk. 0.62 of head-span is the observed motion, not a safe number: it was cut to 0.22 once to stop the neck tearing at the shoulder, which fixed the tear by deleting the motion (SSIM 0.9824, a still with a tremor) and was judged 'nothing believable'. THE TEAR IS STRUCTURAL, NOT NUMERIC. It was held together by four channels — bob, bobCollar, bobBeak, bobEye — each independently declaring this same amplitude, duration and easing, so agreement was a coincidence maintained by hand and any divergence opened the bird at the neck. Neck, collar, beak and eye are now carriedBy the head in the depiction: they have NO motion of their own and are displaced by this track, so the join cannot open.

channels.name: tailFlick
channels.note: Inherited from pp:Bird, where it was declared and never consumed. Degrees, not a fraction — a rotation has no part width to be a fraction of.

channels.name: blink
channels.note: The one motion a rig row cannot state: a cycle repeats forever and a blink has an end. On the duration scale (100/150ms), like pp:Character's — a timing system means every interval is drawn from one set of values.

concepts.label: Tree
concepts.note: The trunk is declared below the foliage so the canopy paints over it and they read as one plant.

channels.name: sway
channels.note: The canopy moves and the trunk does not, which is the whole difference between a tree in wind and a picture of a tree sliding. 1200ms because its 400/800 split is the only period besides 800 whose halves both sit on the duration scale.

channels.name: drift
channels.note: A cloud has no articulation; it only goes somewhere. Declaring drift as a shift says exactly that, and says it in the same vocabulary a head turn and a bus use.

concepts.label: Place
concepts.note: A setting the subject occupies. Unlike an object it is drawn at the size of the frame, and it is created FIRST — everything else stands in it.

concepts.label: Room
concepts.note: A corner and a skirting board are what separate a room from two flat bands.

channels.name: daylight
channels.note: The glass is the brightest thing in an interior and the first to answer the hour. A transform, so the room changes rather than cuts.

concepts.label: Vehicle
concepts.note: Wheels are declared BELOW the body so the body paints over their tops and they read as tucked under it rather than stuck on.

channels.name: jounce
channels.note: Suspension. The body, its glazing and its trim lift together and the wheels do not — that gap IS the suspension, and it is why the three are one channel naming three parts rather than three channels that can drift apart.

channels.name: travel
channels.note: A vehicle moves as one rigid thing, so travel is the same rigid shift a head turn is. One beat with a long `until` crosses smoothly; consecutive beats would glide back to rest between them, because every shift beat re-anchors at zero.

rig.note: Wheels turn while the vehicle travels.

concepts.label: Building
concepts.note: A roof without a facade under it is a floating triangle; the facade is what makes it a building.

channels.name: lightUpper
channels.note: A window is dark until someone is behind it. As a transform it comes up over 300ms rather than cutting, which is what a filament or a lamp being switched on actually looks like.

channels.name: lightLower
channels.note: The other window, declared separately so a row of houses can light unevenly — which is the only thing that makes a row read as inhabited rather than switched.

concepts.label: Criterion
concepts.note: Evaluative. Carries no geometry — it is how work is judged, not something drawn.

concepts.label: Rubric axis
concepts.note: One of the seven axes Goal 1 names. A piece is judged on these and nothing else.

concepts.label: Hierarchy
concepts.note: one clear focal point with tiers beneath it

concepts.label: Contrast
concepts.note: text legible against what is behind it; elements distinguishable

concepts.label: Alignment
concepts.note: a grid, and the frame used deliberately

concepts.label: Restraint
concepts.note: few things carrying the composition, most of the frame calm

concepts.label: TimingRhythm
concepts.note: pace and holds, rather than everything arriving at once

concepts.label: MotionPurpose
concepts.note: what changes communicates, rather than decorates

concepts.label: Palette
concepts.note: a disciplined palette with one accent

concepts.label: Anti-pattern
concepts.note: A named failure observed in this pipeline's own output, with the measurement that catches it. Goal 1(d) is zero of these in shipped work.

concepts.label: A crowd at one visual weight
Two captions in the same place
concepts.note: occludedTextFraction, text counted as an occluder

concepts.label: A long piece that is one held composition
A picture in the corner of the frame it declared
concepts.note: bounds underfill on the trimmed span

concepts.label: A background that becomes the film
The renderer's own artboard in frame
concepts.note: compare the two rasterizers on one bare scene

concepts.label: The engine's placeholder shipped as copy
Domain
concepts.note: What KIND of work a piece is. Gold is per-domain: a typographic exemplar says nothing about an illustration, so a piece is only ever compared within its own.

concepts.label: Character
concepts.note: A figure that can PERFORM. It is baked as FEATURES rather than expressions — each eye, the mouth, the rest of the face — because a feature can be transformed and an expression can only be swapped. A gesture is a deformation of one node with an attack, a hold and a release; that is what a swap between two drawings throws away, and the missing middle is what reads as flashing however well the two ends are chosen.

channels.name: blink
channels.note: The eyes close by flattening, which is what a lid does. As a transform it eases shut and open; as a swap it could only cut, and a cut on a 110ms gesture is the whole gesture. Timings sit on the duration scale (100/150ms) rather than near it: a system of a few durations is what separates motion design from things moving, and 100/150 is still a blink.

channels.name: say
channels.note: One mouth, opened and closed. Real lip sync needs word timings from a voice track; this is the shape of speech and is honest about being that. On the duration scale, for the same reason as the blink.

channels.name: headTurn
channels.note: A head turn moves the HEAD. It named no part, and a shift with no part moved every part of the figure — which was invisible here because pp:Character is a portrait with no body, so 'the whole figure' and 'the head' are the same set. On a figure that has a body (pp:Peep has body_0..2) the same channel slides the whole person sideways. Naming head_0 narrows it, and the face, hair and eyelids are carriedBy head_0, so they travel with it instead of being left behind.

concepts.label: Open Peeps figure
concepts.note: A figure drawn from the Open Peeps corpus (Pablo Stanley, CC0). Its face arrives as ONE compound path whose subpaths cut holes in each other, so the eyes cannot be separated out without destroying the drawing — measured: four of twelve faces lost their mouth when that was tried. It therefore blinks with LIDS laid over the face instead of by flattening an eye, which is why it needs its own blink channel rather than pp:Character's.

channels.name: blink
channels.note: A lid that FADES in over 100ms rather than one that scales down over the eye. scaleY was the better gesture and it does not survive the pipeline: a resting scale is dropped by addItem, by the character handler AND by the engine's own item construction, so the lid rendered at full height and sat over the eye. Opacity is carried end to end and was already proven by the alternate channels. Inverted against pp:Character's blink for the same reason as before: that one flattens an eye, this one brings a lid over it.

concepts.label: Open Doodles figure
concepts.note: A whole figure in a POSE — dancing, running, reading, meditating. Open Peeps ships one body and dresses it, so a Peep can only stand; a story needs someone doing something. Drawn as flat shapes with no separable eye, so it does not blink: it acts.

concepts.label: Drawn face — construction method
concepts.note: HOW TO BUILD A FACE THAT READS, as a method rather than a drawing. Adapted from 'All my friends are made of JavaScript' (Nikolaj Sokolowski), which produces faces that read as hand-drawn using nothing this renderer lacks. Three separations, and the discipline is keeping them apart. IDENTITY: one seed decides the skull, the rest pose, which features and which colours — derived in a fixed order and only ever APPENDED to, so an existing face never changes when a new trait is added. MOTION: what the head is doing right now — turn, gaze, blink, mouth — computed as numbers, with no drawing in it, so the same pose is reproducible and cheap. STYLE: how both of those look. A new style must not reinvent the motion. The payoff is that a face becomes parameters instead of artwork: it can turn, blink and speak because nothing about it was baked into a picture. MARKS: draw contours as filled ribbons that taper at the ends, not as constant-width strokes — see the illustration vocabulary. A face assembled from perfect capsules reads as a diagram.
